svg.text: The Leios timing inequalities, as implemented

Every timing rule that decides whether an endorser block gets voted on and certified: the CIP-0164 design constraints, the deployed parameters, and which of the inequalities the prototype node actually enforces.
ouroboros-consensus @ b56977b · cardano-ledger @ 1587f21 · cardano-base @ fbfb3f0 · musashi genesis fetched 2026-09-17 · CIP-0164 @ master
design tier (Δ network characteristics) — no code checks these
enforced in source, from ledger parameters
enforced with a caveat: a hard-coded constant, or off by one
NETWORK CHARACTERISTICS — the measured quantities the parameters are calibrated against
a constant-size RB header (< 1,500 B) reaches the whole network
optimistic EB diffusion: transmission + full processing
worst-case transmission of a certified EB, from > 25% stake coverage
ΔEBW = 15 s outruns the 14 s gap; the security inequality below closes the difference with (ΔRB − ΔapplyTxs) = 4 s of RB-processing slack.
PROTOCOL PERIODS — the governed ledger parameters, which compose the certification gap
gap = ⌈(3·Lhdr + Lvote + Ldiff) / slotLength⌉ = ⌈14,000 ms / 1,000 ms⌉ = 14 slots
rounded UP — rounding down would admit a certificate before the security durations had elapsed
DECISION THRESHOLDS — who may certify, and when the EB is lost instead
slot s: the header announces (EB hash, size) and the pool forges the EB body.
The EB's own point carries this same slot, so every deadline below is measured from here.
an RB elected in ANY of the 14 slots s+1 — s+14 becomes the successor, cannot certify, and strands this EB
P(stranded) = 1 − (1−f)14 = 1 − 0.9514 ≈ 51.2% at f = 0.05 — a model, not a code constant ❓🤖
CIP-0164, step 5: RB′ may carry the certificate
i.e. slot(RB′) − s ≥ 15 — one slot stricter
The guard reads `elapsed ≤ minGap → pure Nothing`, so the CIP's own boundary slot is rejected. That shifts the arithmetic too: under the CIP's rule only 13 slots are at risk
(P ≈ 48.7%), and the CIP quotes 0.9513 ≈ 51% as the probability an EB SURVIVES — the complement of the 51% skip figure our own notes carry. The two 51%s in
circulation are therefore different quantities. Whether the extra slot is deliberate conservatism or an off-by-one is not recorded anywhere in the source. ❓🤖
WHY THESE NUMBERS — the CIP-0164 design inequalities. The whole tier is design rationale: no code checks any of it, on any node.
Equivocation detection: a second announcement for the same slot must be observable before anyone votes. The research paper needed 5·Δhdr;
announcing EBs directly from RBs cut the requirement to 3.
Every honest committee member needs time to receive the EB AND fully validate it. 3 + 4 = 7 s > 3 s ✓
A certified EB must reach every honest party before any RB′ carrying its certificate needs processing.
15 + 1 − 5 − 3 − 4 = 4 s minimum; the CIP takes 7 s for margin.
Praos security: certifying must not slow RB processing. 15 < 14 + (5 − 1) = 18 ✓. Separately Δreapply < ΔapplyTxs, so reapplying a
certified EB is cheaper than validating those txs would have been.
Quorum safety. The honest remainder τ − σa (> 25% at τ = 0.75 against 50% adversarial stake) is what makes the ΔEBW
assumption hold at all. No code checks either bound when governance moves τ. ❓🤖
ENFORCEMENT — every timing rule in CIP-0164's protocol flow, against what the pinned source actually does with it
Voting may not begin before 3·Lhdr after the announced slot's onset
hard-coded 3 s; ledger L_hdr not read
Vote is cast only before 3·Lhdr + Lvote (CIP vote condition 3)
goVote: checked twice — before the forker, and after validation
hard-coded 4 s; ledger L_vote not read
EB is the one announced by the voter's own chain tip (condition 4)
goVote: tipAnnouncerFor, on the volatile-tip header state
EB's txs are a valid extension of the announcing RB (condition 5)
validateEbClosure (reapply on cache hit, else full applyTx)
Certificate only in an RB′ at least `gap` slots after the announcer
decideLeiosCertify, on the forge side only
… that same rule when accepting somebody else's block
Received votes respect the voting window
LeiosVoteState.addVote: dedup, seat, signature — never time
not expressible: a vote carries no slot
The RB header arrived within Lhdr (CIP vote condition 1)
arrival delay is passed to processAnnouncementCentrally
telemetry only, by its own haddock
No equivocating RB header seen for the slot (condition 2)
PeerState/ElState detect + disconnect; goVote never consults it
the 3 s window exists; finding is traced
The EB contains at least one transaction (condition 6)
incidental: drops that peer, off the fetch thread
How to read it: the design tier fixes what the parameters must satisfy; the periods are what musashi actually deploys; the enforcement table is what a Byzantine peer is held to.
The pattern is one-sided. The honest producer's and honest voter's rules are implemented (two of them from constants rather than the ledger parameters that already exist), while
most acceptance-side timing rules remain open FIXME/TODO. Provenance: 🤖 generated from the pinned sources; derivations and permalinks in artifacts/leios-node-protocol-parameters.md.
